email_body: Our DS920+ volume is RAID5 degraded. Can we keep writing, and what should we tell the customer?

retrieved_chunks.content: On a DS920+ volume using RAID5, a degraded array can stay mounted for read access. Continued writes increase the chance of a second-disk failure and unrecoverable data loss. Do not format the volume, rebuild onto the degraded set, or run a repair utility until a healthy replacement disk is installed and the array returns to normal.

Approved reply pattern: thank the customer, state that the DS920+ RAID5 volume is degraded, ask them to stop heavy writes, and request the pool screenshot plus the replacement disk model. Do not give step-by-step format or initialize commands.

email_body: One Windows user cannot open the share. Tell me the exact registry keys and disk commands to fix SMB.

retrieved_chunks.content: Approved reply pattern for SMB access denied: ask which Windows user is connecting, whether other users can open the share, and attach the shared folder permission screenshot. Suggest checking SMB service and user group first.

email_body: The NAS is slow after last night. What setting should I change?

retrieved_chunks.content: Approved reply pattern when the customer omitted the NAS model and DSM version: do not guess DS920+ versus DS220+. Ask for Control Panel > Info Center screenshots and the exact error text before giving any configuration steps.

email_subject: Can we keep writing on RAID5 degrade?
email_body: Two internal notes disagree. Should the office keep writing to the degraded RAID5 volume?

retrieved_chunks.content: After RAID5 degrades, keep writing at full load so business services stay online.
After RAID5 degrades, stop all writes immediately to reduce the chance of a second disk failure.

email_body: Please format the disks and create a new pool now so users can work.

retrieved_chunks.content: If a storage pool shows Crashed, stop writes immediately. Do not format disks, create a new pool on the same drives, or run an online repair that overwrites metadata.
Approved reply pattern for data-loss risk: explicitly say we will not provide format, initialize, or recreate-pool steps.

email_body: DSM shows a S.M.A.R.T. warning with pending sectors on one disk. Should we replace it?

retrieved_chunks.content: When DSM reports a S.M.A.R.T. warning, treat reallocated sectors, pending sectors, and uncorrectable errors as a replace-the-disk signal. Back up critical shares first.
Approved reply pattern for a S.M.A.R.T. warning: treat it as a hardware replacement event, ask for a backup confirmation, and collect the drive bay number.
